response:
READING

**The fixed cost is identical and can be set aside**

Both courses put ten technicians through the same learning curve, generating roughly the same 28 extra remakes each, for a total of GBP 27,072. That sum neither favours nor disfavours either course. I set it aside and focus on what is actually different.

---

**What KIRKBANE costs that AVENSWOOD does not**

KIRKBANE adds GBP 44,000 in overtime. That is a certain, contracted spend. In return it buys operational simplicity (one library, one system, no crossing remakes) and a clean completion date of 2027-12-04.

---

**What AVENSWOOD costs that KIRKBANE does not**

*Cross-system remakes.* The pilot pair generated 40 of these in four months: 2 technicians, 10 old-system colleagues, 8 "tech-months" of dual-system exposure, at roughly 5 extra remakes per tech-month. Under AVENSWOOD the exposure is heavier in the middle and lighter at both ends, but the nine-month dual period never approaches the arithmetic needed to match GBP 44,000.

Working through the three AVENSWOOD cohorts:

| Period | New-system techs in transition | Duration | Approx tech-months | Est. crossing remakes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jan–Apr 2027 | 3 | 3 months | 9 | ~45 |
| Apr–Jul 2027 | 6 | 3 months | 18 | ~90 |
| Jul–Oct 2027 | 9 | 3 months | 27 | ~135 |

That gives roughly 270 crossing remakes as an upper bound (the pilot rate applied uniformly, which overstates it because the rate depends on both populations, and the old-system population shrinks fast in the third cohort). At GBP 96 each: **~GBP 26,000 worst case**. A more conservative scaling—holding the crossing-remake rate proportional to the product of both populations—gives closer to GBP 11,000–16,000. Either way, the threshold at which crossing remakes would match the GBP 44,000 overtime is 458 remakes. Nothing in the data supports reaching that number.

*Dual shade and material libraries for nine months.* This is a real maintenance overhead and a real error-risk. It is not zero. But the problem notes that practices already work from Wearmouth's library, so the main risk is internal consistency rather than external communication, and it is manageable.

---

**The practice-relationship dimension**

The financial comparison already favours AVENSWOOD, but the quality-exposure argument makes the case stronger.

Under KIRKBANE, 10 of 12 technicians start at 11.4% simultaneously. Lab-wide remake rate from day one: roughly (2/12 × 3.1%) + (10/12 × 11.4%) = **~10%**, against the settled 3.1%. All 40 practices see this at the same moment, in the same month. For a business whose revenue and reputation rest on forty relationships, a threefold spike in remake rate across the entire client base simultaneously is a meaningful commercial risk, regardless of whether overtime keeps unit count up.

Under AVENSWOOD, the worst-case lab-wide remake rate (first cohort arrives, January 2027) is roughly (5/12 × 3.1%) + (3/12 × 11.4%) + (4/12 × 3.1%) ≈ **5%**—still elevated, but not tripled, and spread across a fraction of caseload. By the second cohort the total lab is producing more from the new system, but the proportion still at par or near-par is three-quarters of the bench throughout.

---

**Deadline check**

Both courses finish the migration well before the 2028-06-30 Kessendale end-of-support date. KIRKBANE completes by 2027-12-04; under AVENSWOOD the last technician starts on the new system on 2027-10-04, so the old system is decommissioned nine months ahead of the deadline. Deadline pressure does not change the choice.

---

**Does KIRKBANE's operational simplicity earn back GBP 44,000?**

The case for it would need one or more of: (a) dual-library errors materially exceeding GBP 18,000 in net cost, (b) cross-system remakes substantially above the estimates above, or (c) management overhead of running two systems being worth the difference. None of these close the gap to GBP 44,000. The savings from not paying overtime, combined with a lower peak quality impact and a phased learning-curve that keeps experienced technicians alongside those in training, make AVENSWOOD the sounder choice.

---

CALL
  AVENSWOOD

GROUNDS
  The GBP 44,000 overtime that KIRKBANE requires is not recovered by its operational simplicity, because cross-system remake costs under AVENSWOOD are bounded well below that figure by the pilot data, and AVENSWOOD avoids simultaneously exposing all forty practices to a lab-wide remake rate of roughly ten percent.
